subtitle: std::span<ElementType, Extent> — C++20's non-owning view over a contiguous sequence, back-ported by re_std to C++11 (a back-port of the C++20 surface). A fixed-extent span stays the size of a single pointer via internal::span_storage<T, Extent>; the dynamic_extent specialisation additionally tracks a run-time size. The full accessor / observer / subview API (front, back, operator[], data, size, size_bytes, empty, begin/end, rbegin/rend, first/last/subspan in both fixed-extent-template and dynamic forms, with compile-time extent propagation) ships from C++11, and is constexpr from C++11 — RE_STD AHEAD OF STD, which did not make span constexpr until C++20. The reverse-iterator factories are the one constexpr exception: they become constexpr only at C++17, matching re_std::reverse_iterator's own constexpr-ness. The practical constructor set (default, pointer+count, pointer+pointer, C-array, re_std::array, converting/extent-erasing span) ships from C++11 using SFINAE-constrained constructor templates. The byte views as_bytes / as_writable_bytes are gated at C++17 (the lowest tier with std::byte) and are non-constexpr on every tier (reinterpret_cast). The CTAD deduction guides are a C++17 language feature and cannot be back-ported further. The C++20 contiguous-range constructor span(R&&) and the ranges borrowed-range / view opt-ins are deferred pending re_std::ranges. span has no relationship to <string_view>; the two modules are independent.
legend_blurb: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <span> header (C++20). Implemented; class + subviews on C++11+ and constexpr from C++11 (ahead of std), byte views and CTAD on C++17+. The ranges borrowed/view opt-ins and the contiguous-range constructor are deferred pending re_std::ranges.

symbols.name: span<T,Extent>
symbols.notes: Lives in span.hpp; whole-file gated on D_ENV_LANG_IS_CPP11_OR_HIGHER. Storage is internal::span_storage<T, Extent>: the fixed-extent primary holds only the pointer (size is the compile-time Extent, so a fixed span is pointer-sized), and a partial specialisation for Extent == dynamic_extent additionally stores the run-time size — the same layout split libstdc++/libc++ use. iterator is a raw T* (matches both vendors); reverse_iterator is re_std::reverse_iterator<iterator>. Member types: element_type, value_type (remove_cv<T>), size_type, difference_type, pointer, const_pointer, reference, const_reference, plus the static extent constant (out-of-class definition emitted only on pre-C++17 tiers for ODR; implicitly inline from C++17). Constructors: default (SFINAE'd to participate only when Extent is 0 or dynamic_extent), pointer+count, pointer+pointer, C-array (extent-matching SFINAE), re_std::array& and const re_std::array& (qualification-conversion check via is_convertible<U(*)[], element_type(*)[]>), and a converting/extent-erasing span ctor. RE_STD AHEAD OF STD: the single-return accessors (size, size_bytes, empty, data, operator[], front, back, begin, end) and the first/last/subspan subview family are constexpr from C++11 (std waited for C++20); subspan<Offset, Count> propagates the resulting extent at compile time. The reverse-iterator factories rbegin/rend are constexpr only from C++17 (gated via a local D_SPAN_REV_CONSTEXPR) because std::reverse_iterator is not constexpr-constructible before C++17. DEFERRED: the C++20 contiguous-range constructor span(R&&) is omitted pending re_std::ranges (the practical pointer/array/span ctors cover the common cases); cbegin/cend/crbegin/crend (added to span in C++23) are not yet exposed.
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98. The module is whole-file gated at C++11 per re_std's policy for C++11-introduced / C++20-back-ported view types; concretely the constrained constructors (C-array, re_std::array, converting-span) use SFINAE via default template arguments on constructor templates, a C++11 feature with no equivalent C++98 spelling for constructors through the same mechanism. A C++98 back-port via an extra defaulted function parameter is theoretically possible but was judged not worth a divergent constructor signature set, especially since the wider span surface (CTAD, byte views, the range constructor) tops out at C++17 / C++20 regardless.

symbols.name: dynamic_extent
symbols.notes: Lives in dynamic_extent.hpp. Defined as static_cast<size_t>(-1) to avoid a <limits> dependency; identical in value to numeric_limits<size_t>::max(). Exposed as an inline constexpr variable on C++17+ (ODR-safe, external linkage, matches std) and as a plain constexpr namespace-scope constant on C++11/14 (internal linkage), which is sufficient since it is only ever consumed by value as a template argument or in comparisons.
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98 only because it ships inside the C++11-gated <span> module. The constant itself ((size_t)-1) needs no language feature and would be a plain static const size_t on C++98; it is held at the module's C++11 floor for consistency rather than any intrinsic blocker.

symbols.name: as_bytes
symbols.notes: Lives in as_bytes.hpp; gated on D_ENV_LANG_IS_CPP17_OR_HIGHER. Returns span<const std::byte, (Extent == dynamic_extent ? dynamic_extent : sizeof(T) * Extent)>, computing the byte extent at compile time for fixed-extent inputs. Implemented via reinterpret_cast<const std::byte*>(s.data()) with s.size_bytes() as the length.
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98–C++14: std::byte is a C++17 type, so the result span<const std::byte, ...> is unspellable below C++17. Not constexpr on any tier because reinterpret_cast is never a constant expression (true of std::as_bytes as well).

symbols.name: as_writable_bytes
symbols.notes: Lives in as_writable_bytes.hpp; gated on D_ENV_LANG_IS_CPP17_OR_HIGHER. Mirror of as_bytes returning a mutable span<std::byte, ...>, constrained to non-const element types via re_std::enable_if<!re_std::is_const<T>::value> (matches std's Mandates: !is_const_v<element_type>).
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98–C++14: requires the C++17 std::byte type. Not constexpr on any tier (reinterpret_cast).

symbols.name: span deduction guide
symbols.notes: Defined at the bottom of span.hpp; gated on D_ENV_LANG_IS_CPP17_OR_HIGHER. Five guides: from T(&)[N] -> span<T,N>, from array<T,N>& -> span<T,N>, from const array<T,N>& -> span<const T,N>, from (T*, size_t) -> span<T>, and from (T*, T*) -> span<T>. The std range guide span(R&&) -> span<remove_reference_t<ranges::range_reference_t<R>>> is omitted pending re_std::ranges.
symbols.failure_reason: CTAD (class template argument deduction) is a C++17 language feature; cannot be back-ported. C++11–C++14 users specify the element type and extent explicitly: re_std::span<int, 5> s(arr);

symbols.name: ranges::enable_borrowed_range<span>
symbols.notes: The specialisation that marks span as a borrowed range (its iterators remain valid independently of the span object's lifetime). Deferred: the re_std::ranges customisation-point variable template it specialises has not shipped yet. BACKFILLED 2026-08-25 in span/span_range_opt_in.hpp, a separate header so span.hpp need not depend on <ranges>.
symbols.failure_reason: Ships at C++11, which is below the workbook C++98 floor. This is the floor question, not a coverage gap: the module is currently gated on C++11 and has no C++98 path yet. That is tracked work, not an unreachable tier -- RE_STD_AGENT_README states re_std compiles on C++98 through C++26, and its known-issues table logs blanket C++11 gating (any.hpp) as planned work. See the OPEN tier-floor item.

symbols.name: ranges::enable_view<span>
symbols.notes: The specialisation that marks span as a view (cheap to copy, non-owning). Deferred for the same reason as enable_borrowed_range — depends on the re_std::ranges customisation-point infrastructure. BACKFILLED 2026-08-25 in span/span_range_opt_in.hpp.
